review.summary: Reject: this is drifting into a wooden shutter/door. The reference has closely spaced uniform narrow slats across the full panel, while a large left section is nearly plain and the remaining slats are fewer/wider. Rear lock/handle-like hardware is also invented. Regenerate the full-width architectural slat pattern with only plain rear support battens.

issues.problem: Substantial left portion lacks the repeated slats; overall spacing/count differs strongly from the defining reference pattern.
Unrequested handle/lock-like details make the wall panel read as a door.

review.summary: Reject: invented door hardware is gone, but the clean framed front is now almost a solid flat plate. Slat relief appears only on the rear face beneath cross battens. The reference requires an unobstructed, full-width narrow-slat front, so the defining geometry is still missing.

issues.problem: Nearly all front slat relief is missing; no face provides the reference slatted front without rear support bars crossing it.

review.summary: Reject the first reduction: front slat field gains conspicuous crumpled/faceted neutral shading and wavering edges not present in the high-density source. The accepted m3 geometry/material should be retained while the Blender reduction/normal treatment is changed.

issues.part: front slat field and lower frame
issues.problem: New wrinkled/faceted shading and waviness appear after reduction, degrading the straight repeated pattern.

review.summary: Second reduction retains the same new front-face corrugated/faceted shading and wavering trim. Both bounded reduction attempts are preserved; a separate normal-correction copy is required without further TRELLIS generation.

issues.problem: Persistent reduction-induced shading wrinkles absent from the accepted source.

review.summary: Reference, contact views and full hero inspected. Warm wood tone and dark narrow joints now make the full front slat field legible and consistent with the intended panel. Rear battens and slats use coherent wood materials; no invented hardware remains.

issues.problem: Small source geometry pits remain along the left edge and one rear slat region.

review.summary: Third candidate restores uniform full-width front slat divisions while keeping the outer frame and rear support battens; invented door hardware is absent. All clay views and full hero checked. Ray-cast cross sections confirm repeated front grooves, unlike the almost flat m2 front, so the pattern is real geometry.

issues.problem: Front groove relief is shallow and a few small pits remain on the left frame edge; inspect wood material and reduced output closely.
